scores.evidence: On a timeout, query the PSP for the payment's state before any retry; never retry blindly.
scores.rationale: Technical claims about PCI SAQ-A scope, outbox semantics, at-least-once delivery with consumer dedupe, RLS enforcement, and SERIALIZABLE ledger postings are all accurate, including the subtle areas.

scores.evidence: If you only mean billing for *one* SaaS product's subscribers, the build-vs-buy gate flips.
scores.rationale: Explicitly resolves the key ambiguity, covers catalog, subscriptions, usage, invoicing, payments, dunning, tax and reconciliation, and defers scope with stated triggers.

scores.evidence: Strong consistency (CP) for money... Availability first (AP) for usage ingestion: accept events, dedupe later.
scores.rationale: Consistency choices, module boundaries, data ownership and the outbox-based flows are applied uniformly across every phase with no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: Fault injection (PSP timeout after the charge succeeded, duplicate webhooks, reversed webhook order) causes zero double charges in 10k runs.
scores.rationale: Each phase has checkable exit criteria tied to the specific risks (property-tested balancing, cross-tenant suite, golden invoices, live $1 charge), and reconciliation plus invariant metrics continue in production.

scores.evidence: Interpretation (stated, not assumed): This is a billing platform where each tenant is a business with its own catalog, customers and invoices
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit, numeric thresholds are framed as revisit triggers rather than facts, and the plan states exactly which assumptions would flip the design.

scores.evidence: Tax provider down → invoice stays draft and is retried behind a circuit breaker; tax is never guessed.
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures — double charges, duplicate/out-of-order webhooks, late usage events, cross-tenant leaks, noisy tenants, insider adjustments — each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: Dashboard of reconciliation differences that pages on any unexplained difference.
scores.rationale: Deployment, migrations (expand-then-contract), domain-meaningful metrics, alerts and drills are concrete, but rollback procedure and incident ownership/on-call structure are only implicit.

scores.evidence: Buy: payment processing and card tokenization (Stripe or Adyen, which keeps us in PCI SAQ-A scope)
scores.rationale: Build-vs-buy trade-offs and PSP-fee triggers are reasoned well, but there are no build/run cost estimates, no people-cost sizing, and no discussion of how infrastructure cost grows with usage.

scores.evidence: Money representation (irreversible)... None. This cannot be changed later without restating history.
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions (money format, ledger model, API contract) are flagged and validated early, while reversible ones get explicit revisit triggers and isolation (payments interface, cell migration path).

scores.evidence: Modular monolith with enforced module boundaries... Pull usage ingestion out into its own service when it needs different scaling
scores.rationale: Starts with the simplest workable design, defers microservices, multi-currency, second PSP and rev-rec behind concrete triggers, and omits no essential billing capability.

scores.evidence: An internal "house" tenant calls POST /v1/invoices with its API key and an Idempotency-Key.
scores.rationale: Phases are ordered by stated dependencies, the first slice is fully concrete down to the request/response, and every phase has measurable exit checks a team could execute immediately.

checklist.evidence: Store amounts as integer minor units (bigint) with an ISO 4217 currency code on every amount... Rounding is half-even at the line-item level
Double-entry, append-only and immutable. Corrections are reversing entries and credit notes, never UPDATEs.
Inbound webhook processor: signature verified, deduped, and tolerant of out-of-order delivery because the state machine guards every update.
PSP-hosted card fields keep us in PCI SAQ-A scope... Webhook signatures checked with a replay window... Refunds and disputes as ledger postings.
RLS on every table, app role without BYPASSRLS... tenant A's key cannot read or write tenant B's data through any endpoint
tenant-supplied event ID, dedupe window, timestamp rules, late-arrival policy... Replaying the raw S3 events reproduces the aggregates byte-for-byte.
Products and immutable price versions. A price is frozen once any invoice uses it... Proration rules for upgrades, downgrades and mid-cycle changes.
Gapless invoice numbering per tenant, for compliance... Tax-provider integration. The response is snapshotted onto the invoice.
Dunning: versioned retry schedules, then past_due and cancel... Hosted customer portal: update payment method
Daily reconciliation of the ledger against PSP balance and payout reports, with a queue of differences.
Entitlements and feature-gating service. Pull forward when more than 3 tenants ask to check access through our API instead of webhooks.
Buy: payment processing and card tokenization... tax calculation... Build: ledger, rating, subscriptions and invoicing. That is the product.

traps.evidence: Store amounts as integer minor units (bigint) with an ISO 4217 currency code on every amount.
Finalized invoices are immutable (DB trigger)... Credit notes. These are the only way to correct a finalized invoice
The idempotency key is invoice_id:attempt_n... signature verified, deduped, and tolerant of out-of-order delivery
Payment methods stored only as PSP tokens... keeps us in PCI SAQ-A scope because no card numbers touch us
RLS on every table, app role without BYPASSRLS... A cross-tenant suite shows tenant A's key cannot read or write tenant B's data

note: An exemplary billing-platform plan: correct on the hard money/idempotency/isolation problems with trigger-based deferrals; only cost quantification, explicit rollback/incident ownership, and entitlement availability fall short.
